description: Roboto_origin Fully Open-Source DIY Humanoid Robot/萝博头原型机全开源手搓级人形机器人

summary.one_liner: ROBOTO_ORIGIN is an open-source aggregation repo for RoboParty's DIY humanoid robot prototype, pulling together the hardware, deployment, training, firmware and other sub-repositories in one place.
summary.what_it_does: This is a snapshot aggregation repository for the ROBOTO_ORIGIN (RPO) humanoid robot prototype, which the README says was developed and open-sourced by RoboParty, including its structure, electronics, training and deployment work. It does not contain the robot code itself; it links to and periodically syncs eight sub-repositories covering hardware design, ROS2 deployment, RL training in IsaacLab with MuJoCo sim2sim transfer, URDF/MJCF robot descriptions, firmware (USB2CAN, OrangePi/RDK tooling), exterior shell assets, navigation, and XR teleoperation. The README gives a git clone and git pull quick start and says each module under modules/ has its own README. It also points to a Humanoid Robot Know-How documentation set and a QQ community group. The README says a BOM table exists but the table content is not included in the text provided.
use_cases: Build a DIY humanoid robot from open-source hardware files
Train walking and running policies in IsaacLab
Transfer a trained RL policy from IsaacLab to MuJoCo
Deploy robot control software on ROS2
Load a humanoid URDF or MJCF model for simulation
Set up embedded firmware on OrangePi or RDK boards
Run XR teleoperation experiments on the robot
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL shown as empty in the README>
Navigate to modules/<module-name> and follow the README inside that module
notable: Fully open-sourced R&D process, including structure, electronics, training and deployment
Aggregates eight sub-repositories so all resources can be pulled from one place
Direct IsaacLab training workflow with Sim2Sim transfer to MuJoCo
Claims the robot can be assembled from Taobao parts and Jialichuang prototyping
caveats: Snapshot only: issues and code contributions belong in the individual sub-repositories
Some internal package names and paths still use historical Atom01 names
README disclaimer: the software is provided as-is and the operator bears all physical risk from hardware actions
The rpo_appearance shell is for static display only and printing is not recommended
FAQ says basic Linux and ROS2 knowledge is helpful
